The paper evaluates different methods for determining the angle of attack (AoA) and induced velocity on wind turbine blades using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) under axial inflow conditions.
The two 10 MW reference wind turbines used in the study were the INNWIND.EU/DTU and AVATAR turbines.
The free-stream velocities considered were 6 m/s and 9 m/s, with rotor speeds of 6 RPM and 7.3 RPM, respectively.
The computational grid used for the CFD simulations had a total of 14 million cells.
The y+ values at the blade surface were kept below 1 everywhere with a cell size of 2 × 10^-6 normal to the wall.
The results show good agreement between the evaluated methods at the mid-span, though some deviations are observed at the root and tip regions of the blades.
The discrepancies at the root and tip regions are attributed to the 2D assumptions of the methods not capturing the 3D effects of the bound circulation.
The 3-Point method is able to reproduce the dynamic behavior of the induction and AoA near the tip and root of the blade, which is important for yawed flow.
The Shen 2 method has a lower dependency on the monitoring point locations compared to the Shen 1 method, especially near the root.
The CFD results were compared to BEM calculations using FAST V8, where the polars from the CFD computations were used, and no 3D correction models were applied.
The paper aims to assess available methods to extract AoA from CFD simulations, so that CFD results can be used for calibration of induction modelling in BEM.
The investigations were performed for two 10 MW reference wind turbines under axial inflow conditions, namely the turbines designed in the EU AVATAR and INNWIND.EU projects.
The Ellipsis3D CFD solver was used for the numerical simulations, which is a multi-block finite volume discretization of the incompressible Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations.
The computations were performed using the k-ω SST turbulence model and the Drela/Giles version of the En transition model.

The computational grid was fully structured based on hexahedral cells, with 256 cells around the airfoils, 129 cells in the span-wise direction for each blade, and 129 cells in the wall normal direction.
